name: AI agent swarm running back-office operations
description: Reference Trust Requirements Profile for a swarm of AI agents that plans, delegates and executes back-office work and spawns helper agents as it goes. Illustrative draft values.

scope.intended_use: Trust requirements for one swarm of language model agents under a single orchestrator, with tool access, a budget and a human approver for payments.
scope.boundary: One orchestrator, every agent it spawns, their tools, credentials, budget and outbound data paths.
out_of_scope: How the system is scored against these signals
How a halt or other action is enforced
Any claim of regulatory compliance or certification

scored_signals.reason: Agents alive in the swarm. Uncontrolled spawning is how a swarm outgrows its oversight and its budget.
New agents a minute. A burst of spawning precedes most runaway swarms.
Longest chain of agents delegating to agents. Deep chains lose the original instruction and the accountable owner.
Messages between agents a second. Agents answering each other in a loop amplify without limit.
Model and tool spend a minute.
Share of tool calls that fail. A rising rate means the swarm is acting on a broken picture of its systems.
Distance between what the swarm is doing and the objective it was given, scored by an independent monitor. Injected instructions show up here first.
Agreement between agents that check each other's work. Low agreement marks a decision nobody should trust yet.

standing_bands.range: all signals within acceptable operating range and no hard rule met
one or more signals in the warning range
a signal in the critical range, missing evidence, or a hard rule met

required_standing.source_requirement: The goal drift monitor and the evaluation source should be independent of the swarm and its vendor.

notes: Threshold values are illustrative draft values for a demonstration.
Readings in a swarm are stochastic and coupled. Agent count follows spawn rate, and spend follows message rate.
For orientation only, not a compliance claim. Frameworks that address oversight of autonomous AI systems include the EU AI Act provisions on human oversight and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
